column2: Having spoken thus to him, Brahmins, that god, kind to devotees, Vishnu, whose course is hard to know, vanished right there.
When he had gone, best of sages, Kandu, with glad mind, renouncing all desires, became again composed in thought,
restraining all the senses, free of mine-ness and egotism, one-pointed, rightly meditating on that Purushottama,
unstained, free of qualities, peaceful, established as pure being, and attained supreme liberation, hard to get even for the gods.
One who recites or hears the story of the great-souled Kandu is freed from all sins and goes to the heavenly world.
Thus, best of sages, the land of action has been told by me, and the supreme field of liberation and the god Purushottama.
Those who see the Lord, praise the boon-giver, and with devotion meditate on the liberator called Shri-Purushottama, ageless, remover of the sorrows of worldly existence,
having enjoyed kings' pleasures, pure, and divine happiness in heaven, afterwards, free of all faults, go to the imperishable abode of Hari.
The earlier Daitya, the very mighty Hiranyakashipu, was slain; he who formerly became fire, Aurva, the all-destroying lord,
Hari dwelling in Patala drank the essence of the ocean made of water; Brahman of a thousand feet, giving a thousand thousand rays,
the thousand-headed god whom they declare in every yuga, from whose navel a lotus arose, whose is the Grandfather's house,
in the single ocean, in the world of the Nagas, with a golden lotus; by whom those Daityas were slain in the battle of Taraka's making;
by whom, making a divine body bearing all weapons, standing in a cave, the arrogant Kalanemi was felled;
at the end of the north of the sea, in the Milk-ocean's nectar-sea, who sleeps, taking up eternal yoga, in great darkness;
Aditi, mother of gods, bore a divine, ancient embryo through the excess of her austerity, and who made Shakra, who was besieged by the hosts of Daityas, by attention to the embryo;
who, making steps full of yoga, made the Daityas dwell in the waters, and made the gods lords of the thirty and made Puruhuta lord of the gods;
by the Garhapatya procedure, by the Anvaharya rite, the Ahavaniya fire, the Veda, the initiation, firewood, the stable —
the Prokshaniya, the ladle, and likewise the Avabhritha; who made the gods partakers of the share of oblation, with hands downward,
who made the gods eaters of oblation and the ancestors eaters of the funeral offering, and for enjoyment engaged them in sacrificial rite by the sacrificial procedure;
vessels, fee, initiation, charu, mortars, post, firewood, ladle, soma, purifiers and boundary sticks,
sacrificial substances, cups and others, members of the assembly, sacrificers, and the best sacrifices such as Medha —
he who distributed them formerly by the action of the Supreme Lord, who made the worlds in accordance with the yuga by successive valour,
moments, winks, kashthas, kalas, the three times, muhurtas, tithis, months, day and year,
seasons and time-conjunctions, measure threefold in the three, lifespans, fields, growth, marks, beauty of form,
three worlds, three gods, the threefold Veda, three fires, the three times, three actions, three varnas, three qualities —
all worlds were created formerly by that Infinite by action; the creator who is in all beings, having the qualities of all beings,
who delights in yoga by the prior senses of men, who is the ordinance and Lord by yoga of coming and going,
who is the goal of the righteous and the non-goal of those of sinful deeds, the origin of the four varnas and protector of the four varnas,
who knows the four Vedas, the refuge of the four stages of life, who is the region between the directions, sky, earth, wind and fire,
the light consisting of moon and sun, the Lord of yugas, the night-roamer; who is heard as the supreme light and as the supreme austerity,
whom they call the higher and the lower, the highest one with the Supreme Self, the god of the Adityas and the lord who is the destroyer of Daityas,
who at the ends of yugas is the ender and the ender of the ender of worlds, the bridge of world-bridges, the pure of the pure actions,
the knowable of the Veda-knowers, the lord of those of high origin, the Soma among the gentle, the fire among the fiery,
the lordship of Shakras, the austerity of ascetics, the modesty of the well-conducted, the brilliance of the brilliant,
the embodiment of those worthy of embodiment, the goal of those who have goals; from space the wind arises, from wind's life-breath the fire,
from heaven the fire, life-breath; life-breath is fire, Madhusudana. From juice comes blood, from blood flesh is said to come;
from flesh the birth of fat, from fat bone is said; from bone marrow arose, from marrow semen is born;
from semen the embryo arose by action rooted in juice; there the first portion of the waters is called the heap of Soma.
The second heap is called the one born from the warmth of the womb; know semen as of Soma's nature and the menstrual fluid as of fire's nature.
States follow juices; in the seed are moon and fire; semen is in the phlegm group, and blood in the bile group.
The heart is the place of phlegm; bile is established in the navel; the heart in the middle of the body is the seat of the mind, it is remembered.
The space within the navel's cavity — there is the god Fire; mind is to be known as Prajapati; phlegm is conceived as Soma.
Bile is remembered as fire; thus the world consists of fire and Soma. When the embryo is thus under way and has grown like a bubble,
wind entered it, joined with the Supreme Self. Stationed in the body, it divides fivefold and moves again:
prana, apana, samana, udana and vyana. Prana, increasing the Supreme Self in him, goes around;
apana is the lower part of the body, udana the upper half of the embodied; vyana is that by which it is pervaded; samana returns.
Then comes for him the obtaining of the elements, within the range of the senses: earth, wind, space, water and light the fifth.
Established in his senses, they took each its own share. They say the body is earthy and the life-self is wind;
the openings arise from space; flowing arises from water; light is the eyes and heat; the mind is remembered as their self.
Villages and objects are set in motion by his power. Thus the eternal Purusha, creating all these worlds —

How did Vishnu come to humanity in this world of death? This is our doubt, Brahma, this is our great wonder.
brahmapuran:179:64	How did the goal of those with goals take a human body? Vishnu is said by the gods and Daityas to be a supreme wonder.
brahmapuran:179:65	Tell, great sage, the wondrous origin of Vishnu, of famed strength and valour, of immeasurable brilliance.
brahmapuran:179:66	Let the truth of Vishnu, who has become a wonder by action, be told here: how did that god, remover of the gods' distress, the Purushottama,
brahmapuran:179:67	the all-pervading lord of the world, the great lord of all worlds, the god who creates, preserves and ends, who brings happiness to all worlds,
brahmapuran:179:68	imperishable, eternal, infinite, free of decay and growth, unstained, without qualities, subtle, unchanging, spotless,
brahmapuran:179:69	free of all limiting adjuncts, established as pure being, unchanging, all-pervading, eternal, Supreme Self, eternal,
brahmapuran:179:70	immovable, stainless, pervading, ever satisfied, without support, whose greenness is heard of as pure in the Krita yuga,
brahmapuran:179:71	Vaikuntha-hood among the gods, and Krishna-hood among men — of that Lord this deep course of action
brahmapuran:179:72	past and future we wish to hear. This revered lord who is unmanifest, abiding in manifest marks,
brahmapuran:179:73	Narayana, of infinite self, the origin and the imperishable; becoming Narayana, he was Hari, the eternal.
brahmapuran:179:74	Brahma, Shakra, Rudra, Dharma, Shukra, Brihaspati: the lord, whose nature is Pradhana, created Brahma formerly.
brahmapuran:179:75	He, the primal Purusha, created the Prajapatis in the previous kalpa; thus that revered Vishnu, great lord of all worlds, why did Hari go to the Yadu family in this mortal world?

We, this slayer of Vritra, the two Nasatyas and Dasra, this Varuna, these Rudras, Vasus with the Suns, wind, fire and others,
brahmapuran:181:25	all the gods, lord of gods, what is to be done by these and by me, Lord, command it; obeying your command we stand always, free of faults.
Thus praised, the revered Supreme Lord plucked two hairs of his, white and black, best of Brahmins,
and said to the gods: "These two hairs of mine will descend to the surface of the earth and remove the burden and suffering of the earth.
Let all the gods too descend to earth with portions of themselves and fight with the mad great Asuras born earlier.
Then all those Daityas will go to destruction on earth, crushed by various weapons; no doubt.
Devaki, wife of Vasudeva, like a goddess: her eighth embryo, gods, will be this hair of mine.
Descending there, he will cause the death on earth of Kamsa, born of Kalanemi." Having said so, Hari vanished.
Then, he having become invisible, the gods, having bowed to the great-souled one, went to the back of Meru and descended to the earth.
The revered sage Narada told Kamsa that the eighth embryo of Devaki would be on earth.
Kamsa, hearing that from Narada, grew angry and kept Devaki and Vasudeva confined in his house.
Each child as it was born was handed over to Kamsa, as he had said before; Vasudeva too delivered his son thus, Brahmins.
Six embryos, sons of Hiranyakashipu, are renowned; sleep (Nidra), sent by Vishnu, placed them in the womb in order.
Yoganidra, the great illusion of Vishnu, by whose ignorance the whole world is bewildered: Lord Hari said to her:

Go, Nidra, at my command; the six embryos resting in the nether world, bring them one by one into Devaki's womb.
brahmapuran:181:39	When they are killed by Kamsa, then the sinless part named Shesha will be the seventh in her womb, a portion of a portion.
brahmapuran:181:40	In Gokula Rohini, Vasudeva's wife, is staying; at her time of delivery, the embryo is to be taken by you into her womb.
brahmapuran:181:41	The seventh, out of fear of the Bhoja king, through close confinement, people will say the embryo of Devaki fell.
brahmapuran:181:42	By the drawing (sankarshana) of the embryo, he will get in the world the name Sankarshana, a hero like a white mountain peak.
brahmapuran:181:43	Then I shall be conceived in Devaki's auspicious womb; you must go without delay to Yashoda's womb.
brahmapuran:181:44	In the rainy season, in the sky, on the eighth of the dark half, at night I shall be born; and you will be born on the ninth.
brahmapuran:181:45	Vasudeva, his mind impelled by my power, will take me to Yashoda's bed and you, blameless one, to Devaki's.
brahmapuran:181:46	Kamsa will take you, goddess, and throw you on a stone slab of a mountain, and you will take your place in the sky.
brahmapuran:181:47	Then Shakra, bowing to you out of reverence for me, his head bowed in obeisance, will take you as his sister.
brahmapuran:181:48	Then, having slain thousands of Daityas such as Shumbha and Nishumbha, you will adorn the entire earth in many places.
brahmapuran:181:49	You are Bhuti, Sannati, Kirti, Kanti, Prithivi, Dhriti, Lajja, Pushti, Usha and whatever other; you alone are she.
brahmapuran:181:50	Those who call you Arya, Durga, Vedagarbha, Ambika, Bhadra, Bhadrakali, Kshemya, Kshemankari,
brahmapuran:181:51	and praise you morning and afternoon, bowing in form, all their wish will be fulfilled by my grace.
brahmapuran:181:52	Worshipped with offerings of liquor and meat and with food to eat, you, when pleased, will grant men all desires.
brahmapuran:181:53	All of them will be prosperous always by my grace without doubt, undoubtedly. Go, goddess, as said.
At midnight, when Janardana, the support of all, was being born, the clouds thundered softly and the gods showered flowers.
Seeing him, four-armed, like the petals of a blooming blue lotus, with the Shrivatsa on his chest, Anakadundubhi (Vasudeva) praised him.
Having praised him with pleasing words, the greatly wise one, afraid of Kamsa, Brahmins, then petitioned:

You are known, Lord of lords, bearer of conch, discus and mace; this divine form, god, by your grace withdraw.
brahmapuran:182:15	Today, god, this Kamsa will torment me, knowing that you have descended in this my house.
brahmapuran:182:16	He who has infinite forms and all the universe as his form, bears the worlds even in the womb with his body — may that god of gods be gracious, who has revealed an infant form by his maya.
brahmapuran:182:17	Withdraw this four-armed form, Soul of all; let this Kamsa not know your incarnation, destroyer of Daityas.
What was praised by you formerly, wishing for a son, has been fulfilled for you today, goddess, since I was born from your womb.
Having said so, the revered one became silent, best of sages; Vasudeva too took him that night and went out.
The guards there were bewildered by Yoganidra, and the gatekeepers of Mathura, as Anakadundubhi went.
Shesha with his hoods covered Anakadundubhi from the heavy water of the raining clouds that night and went (with him).
Vasudeva, carrying Vishnu, went to the very deep Yamuna, filled with hundreds of whirlpools, and she flowed only knee-deep.
Taking Kamsa's tax he saw there on the bank Nanda and the old cowherds, who had come, at the Yamuna.
At that time Yashoda too, bewildered by Yoganidra, bore that very girl, sages, while the people were bewildered.
Vasudeva too, placing the boy and taking the girl, quickly came to Yashoda's bed, of immeasurable radiance.
Yashoda, awakening, saw the son born, dark like a blue lotus petal, and was exceedingly glad.
Vasudeva, taking the girl to his own house, placed her on Devaki's bed and remained as before.
Then hearing the child's cry the guards suddenly rose and reported Devaki's delivery to Kamsa, Brahmins.
Kamsa quickly came and seized the girl; though restrained, Devaki, close by, cried "Release, release!"
He threw her on a stone slab; thrown, she stood in the sky, took a great form with eight great arms bearing weapons, laughed loudly and said angrily to Kamsa:
What use is throwing me, Kamsa? He has been born who will kill you, formerly the all-in-all of the gods, your death. Having thought this over, quickly do what is good for yourself.
Having said so, the goddess went, adorned with divine garlands and perfumes, praised by Siddhas in the sky as the Bhoja king looked on.
Having thus commanded the Asuras, Kamsa then entered his own house and, without hostility, said to Vasudeva and Devaki:

The embryos of you two were killed by me in vain; some other boy has arisen for my destruction.
brahmapuran:183:10	Enough of grief; surely that which is to be will be. Who among your children is not killed at the end of life?
Thus consoling and releasing them, Kamsa, having satisfied them, best of Brahmins, entered again his own inner house.
Nanda the cowherd, taking cow-dung, gave protection on Krishna's head and said:

May Hari, origin of all beings, protect you, from whose navel-lotus the world arose;
brahmapuran:184:15	by whom the earth is supported on the tip of his tusk, may that god in the form of Varaha, Keshava, protect you.
brahmapuran:184:16	May Vishnu protect your private parts and belly, Janardana your shanks and feet, and Vamana, who was born in an instant, always protect you.
brahmapuran:184:17	May Govinda, whose weapons flash across the three worlds by Trivikrama's stride, guard your head, and Keshava your neck.
brahmapuran:184:18	May Narayana, the imperishable, of unobstructed lordship, protect your face, arms, forearms, mind and all senses.
brahmapuran:184:19	May Vaikuntha protect you in the directions, Madhusudana in the intermediate directions, Hrishikesha in the sky, and Mahidhara on earth.
Thus, with the blessing performed by Nanda the cowherd, the boy was laid under the cart on the child's cot.
Those cowherds, seeing the huge body of the dead Putana, then felt great terror and amazement.
Once, lying under the cart, Madhusudana, wanting the breast, flung his feet upward and cried.
By the blow of his feet the cart was overturned; its vessels and pots shattered, it fell upside down.
Then all the cowherds and cowherdesses, Brahmins, cried "Alas!" and came, and saw the boy lying on his back.
The cowherds said, "By whom has the cart been overturned?" There the boys said, "It was knocked over by this child.
We saw it, crying, struck by the throw of his feet; the cart was overturned; it was no one else's doing."
Then the cowherds were again very amazed; Nanda the cowherd, greatly astonished, took up the boy.
Yashoda, rising in wonder, worshipped the cart with its broken pots and potsherds with curd, flowers, fruits and unbroken rice.
Garga in Gokula, urged by Vasudeva, performed the naming rites of the two in secret among the cowherds.
The wise Garga, best of the intelligent, named the elder Rama and the other Krishna.
In a short time those two mighty ones, Brahmins, grew and both crawled on knees and hands.
With limbs smeared with dried dung and ashes, roaming here and there, Yashoda and Rohini could not hold them back.
Playing in the middle of the cow-pen and again going to the calf-pen, they were intent on pulling the tails of calves born that day.
When Yashoda was unable to restrain the two children, both going about together, playing and very restless,
she then bound Krishna, of untroubled deeds, with a rope to a mortar in the middle, and said angrily:
If you are able, go, you of restless conduct.
Having said this, the housewife did her own work. While she was busy, he dragged the mortar,
the lotus-eyed one went between the twin arjuna trees, dragging the mortar crosswise between the trees.
By it the tops of the tall branches of the twin arjunas were broken; then, afraid at the sound of crashing,
the people of Vraja came and saw the two great trees fallen, trunks broken, branches broken on the ground.
They saw the boy with a few teeth in his mouth, smiling, standing between them, tightly bound by the rope at his belly.
From the binding with the rope he came to be named Damodara. Then all the old cowherds led by Nanda
took counsel, agitated, fearful of the great portents: "We have no business to stay at this place; let us go to another great forest."
